title: I made a video player and "director" manager, to track and improve engagement for my indie video game
author: jeffyclassify
selftext:
https://i.redd.it/tp53n8ls150i1.png

https://i.redd.it/23bhznjv150i1.png

I've been making an online video game of AI creatures that run their code in your browser. To help understand what users like or not like, I built a cut-scenes manager and player, that also connects with the engagement data of the game, so I can visualize exactly where people are dropping off or skipping

You can think of it as a mix between [Lucas Arts' SCUMM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SCUMM) \+ youtube's viewership/engagement chart overlay that they have on some of their videos + a custom AI agent (connected to Claude Code) to help both: create/improve the storyline, and develop the code for the director UI

  
[Id|le, the game](https://id-le.com?utm_source=r_aigamedev)

[The source code](https://github.com/nicobrenner/id-le)

comments.author: thecrownforge
comments.body: Do you separate people who skip a scene because they saw it before from people who skip it on the first play? I'd also look at what they do right after the scene. A dip there may mean they want control back, not that the story is weak.

replies.author: jeffyclassify
replies.body:
Thank you, those are thoughtful questions. I'm slowly adding more tracking to figure out the different behavior pathways and funnels within the user experience, still early days, but I'll note down your recommendations

Right now I have 3 "arms" for anyone landing on [id-le.com](http://id-le.com) directly without any parameters. So on that video player, I can see engagement either aggregated for all the 3 options, or by each one individually. Currently there's not enough data to apply an optimization algorithm like the multi-armed bandit, so it's just a random uniform split 33.3% probability each. Once I have enough data, I can start doing some optimization on the version selection side, but also tweaking the animations and seeing if I can influence the engagement metrics, especially in moments where users may abandon
